title: An image buffer
hints: Most of the work is one helper: the pointer to the start of row `y` is `pixels + y * stride`. Everything else is loops over rows.

For `blit`, clip first: the visible part of the destination is `subView(destination, x, y, source.width, source.height)`. The matching part of the source starts at column `max(0, -x)` and row `max(0, -y)`.
requirements: All addressing goes through the stride, so sub-views and padded images work.
Blitting clips on all four sides, including negative positions.
Rows are copied with `std::memcpy` and flipped by swapping whole rows.
Nothing outside a view is ever written.
stretch: Add `blitKeyed(destination, x, y, source, transparent)` that skips pixels equal to a transparent colour, and measure how much slower it is than the `memcpy` version on a 1000 by 1000 image.
